edits.title: Diagnose missing biographical fields before further research
edits.content: When structured extraction leaves a biographical field empty, review the stored source specifically for explicit evidence of that field. Distinguish source absence from extraction omission. Do not derive nationality or citizenship from birthplace, education, or workplace. If evidence is absent, retain the unresolved field and search for a source explicitly stating the requested attribute; fetch and verify that evidence before filling the cell. For affiliations, distinguish employment and secondary appointments from educational institutions, and preserve temporal qualifiers such as former or emeritus. Give extraction and review calls the same field definition, time scope, and completeness requirements. If the task uses affiliations recorded in an award announcement, audit those institutions and their stated locations rather than expanding to every outside appointment. Resolve concrete omissions against stored evidence before further searches. Apply this review to unresolved fields without repeating successful searches or downloads.

edits.title: Compare repair results with existing evidence before replacement
edits.content: A targeted re-extraction using only newly fetched sources replaced a supported multi-valued nationality with a narrower value from another person's page navigation. Schema and quote-membership checks passed despite the information loss; recovery required restoring the stronger stored evidence. Supply repair calls with the existing cell and its supporting evidence alongside new evidence. Before replacement, compare source relevance, temporal scope, and every removed or changed component. A source mentioning only one component does not refute the others. Preserve supported components unless evidence justifies their removal, and keep unresolved conflicts explicit. Failed fetches do not invalidate evidence already collected.

The Princeton request failed with HTTP 403 and the TAP request with certificate verification failure. Neither was repeatedly retried. Princeton evidence was replaced by a successfully fetched profile; existing MIT evidence ultimately supported the field sought from TAP. These isolated backend failures support neither permanent domain exclusions nor transport changes. The consequential evidence-replacement regression is addressed separately.

Annual audit responses repeatedly proposed investigating outside advisory and institutional appointments beyond the extraction's announcement scope. The root restored that definition, repaired concrete location and former-status omissions, and obtained a final PASS. Extend the existing diagnostic skill with consistent review scope rather than creating a duplicate workflow.

The nationality-resolution call omitted existing MIT evidence and returned a single nationality from another biography's navigation list. The mutation passed schema and substring checks, then the root explicitly restored the stronger multi-valued cell. Final citation success reflects recovery, not prevention. A memory should preserve this distinct failure mode without retaining person-specific answers.

The initial affiliation quote contained the wrong intervening PDF-column text. The root located the actual passage, copied a contiguous slice, and rechecked membership. The existing PDF memory already describes this exact failure and completed repair procedure; final verbatim checks support retaining it unchanged.

proposal.summary: Update one existing memory to prevent nationality/citizenship drift and unsupported audit corrections. Existing entries already cover fetch failures and honest empty discovery records.

edits.title: Separate quote membership from factual support
edits.content: A quote occurring in model-rendered fetch output does not by itself establish that it is a source quotation or supports the complete claim. Distinguish source excerpts from renderer summaries, headings, labels and assembled passages; do not reject an identified source excerpt solely because the fetch tool renders it. Before recording a positive constraint verdict, verify the entity, required time period and every substantive component of the value against appropriate evidence. Keep extraction and audit criteria aligned with the requested column: explicit national descriptors can support nationality without proving legal citizenship or dual citizenship. Birthplace, ancestry, workplace, flags and unlinked country labels are insufficient substitutes. Preserve explicitly supported compound national descriptors without converting them into citizenship claims. Treat model audit findings as hypotheses to check against saved evidence, not authoritative corrections; distinguish actual additional affiliations from parenthetical organizational descriptions. When different sources support different parts of a composite claim, retain an internal mapping from each claim to its source excerpt and respect the output contract rather than stitching excerpts into a purported verbatim quote. Recheck semantic support after final mutations, even when schema, substring and coverage checks pass.

decisions.reason: All 29 occurrences correspond to empty discovery records: four fallback searches returned already discovered names, nine nationality searches verified known people, eleven gap searches sought missing fields, and five final searches targeted remaining cells. These searches produced useful evidence despite adding no entities. The trajectory inspected results before recording discoveries, unlike the premature-placeholder failure described in the existing memory. Entry 0 already explicitly permits honest empty records for verification searches. Its repeated signal-bearing outcomes therefore do not establish that its procedure is ineffective, and no additional warning or instruction to invent discoveries is warranted.

Reviewed all 26 failures: nine initial NobelPrize.org requests, six initial alternative-source requests, seven nationality requests, two gap requests and two final targeted requests. The nationality batch retried previously failed LIGO and AP URLs; an APS URL that previously succeeded also failed, so neither permanent host outages nor malformed suffixes are established. Two KVA probes succeeded and alternative sources subsequently supported completion. Current entry 1 was already revised to require availability probes before large batches, preserve successful evidence, track failed URLs and avoid unchanged retries. Its usage records concern version 1, not the current version 2; these outcomes do not justify deleting or rewriting the revised procedure. The passing self-check does not erase the wasted requests, but another edit would duplicate existing coverage.

The second audit demanded explicit citizenship for a nationality column; later prompts corrected that criterion and restored an explicitly supported compound national descriptor. Reviews also challenged rendered name–institution lines and later demanded a parent organization as an additional affiliation; focused resolution retained the existing two-institution value. These recoveries show that audit output itself needs evidence checking. Entry 3 already covers quotation provenance and semantic support, but does not clearly distinguish nationality from legal citizenship or guard against unsupported audit corrections. Its update preserves that coverage and adds these specific failure modes. Successful substring checks and complete agent-verdict coverage do not independently validate the reviewers' semantic criteria. Entry 2's saved-evidence repair guidance remains useful and needs no separate edit.
